body: I know your changes didn't introduce it, but might be worth adding a TODO here to mark it more explicitly.

Is there a change that setting the script has unintended consequences? e.g. cause cycle breaks that invalidate the dangling script list, making our own list's reference dangling in turn?
Though, I suppose not, since the list holds strong references.
Is it possible that the function state is changed after clear, leading to the boolean preventing clearing the added state accidentally (potentially creating leaks)?

Looping forever here relies on `set_script(Variant())` to remove the script from the instances.

If any code is ever introduced that rejects removing the script, this will loop forever.

Though to be fair, that would be a major problem for shutdown in general 😅

If it is it would be a bug. We need to clear all function states during language shutdown. If a function state is not cleared but the language is gone, we somehow missed it.

Iirc I added a safety check for the other clear method, with a `GDScript bug (please report)` message. We should probably do the same here, just in case.
Yeah, that's why we copy all scripts into `needs_dangling_clear` and hold strong references.
I guess we could add a check for this just to be sure.

I'm reading "changing the function state" as it getting resumed, since that seems to be the only way to alter it after creation.

If we look at the call graph of `resume` it is only called from `_signal_callback`. Since we clear all incoming connections in `clear` there is no chance of receiving `_signal_callback` after the state was cleared.

So I don't think that's possible.
